question.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/43ffd01ab7a6d78ea0343953b985d9c4165ee76085f345bcd500c053550e3ec9.svg) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/51191f4e8b1417de7b391a71d68c7c5917ed7083cc3b7a630662d6a0912b969c.svg)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/066be34bb8bd7f585bc3d2666007e189f6c82f2e3b7f7a699928066825fd765d.svg)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1})={x}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{1},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1})=\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{2})=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/869b2f5de537961c4c83523ac6fcfd96329fc062e34509d88b8516b7a2259b84.svg)

Evaluating $\boldsymbol{f}$ and its derivative at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/b35d7585ed24aea694c3a31e69c1406744986db30cddf8842a5bae8d6d745e4b.svg) we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/9f3dbb19be577a74b8f19fd1eb5d42910fd0e46637388a3daab80c17d6edd833.svg)

The linear approximation of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf x = \mathbf a$ is given by

$$
\boldsymbol{f}\left(\mathbf x \right) \approx \boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf a) + \boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a)(\mathbf x - \mathbf a).
$$

Substituting $\boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf a),$ $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a),$ and $\mathbf a$ in the equation above, we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/5d526b2485b53b029bc119e66e6a385d0ba228ecca1ffd0c58e7934e83a97a7b.svg)
